organizations.name: Run For Something
organizations.for: young progressives (Millennials and Gen Z) thinking about a first or second run for local or state office
organizations.offers: a call with staff and other would-be candidates, then online trainings, referrals, mentors, and a national network

organizations.name: Working Families Party: Working Class Wins
organizations.for: working people (nurses, drivers, organizers) who want to run as a Working Families Democrat or independent; the party has its own ballot line in New York
organizations.offers: a sign-up to learn the basics of running and how to seek the party's backing, plus training and a network

organizations.name: Emerge
organizations.for: Democratic women thinking about running for office
organizations.offers: a free 90-minute intro session, and state programs such as Emerge Virginia's six-month, 70-hour candidate course

organizations.name: The Collective PAC
organizations.for: progressive Black candidates running at the local, state, or federal level
organizations.offers: an endorsement, with training, technical help, and fundraising support; applications for 2027 races open Dec. 1, 2026

organizations.name: NEA See Educators Run
organizations.for: teachers and school staff in the National Education Association who are running or thinking about it
organizations.offers: a three-day union training on vote goals, your pitch, and building a slate of candidates

organizations.name: Virginia Education Association: Running for Office
organizations.for: VEA members in Virginia's public schools who are thinking about running for state or local office
organizations.offers: a workshop, on request, on whether you're ready, Virginia election and campaign-finance law, organizing, and fundraising

organizations.name: NYSUT Pipeline Project
organizations.for: members of New York State United Teachers who want to run, from school board to the Legislature
organizations.offers: training and help from the union's regional political organizers for members who run

organizations.name: Vote Run Lead
organizations.for: women and gender-expansive people who want to run, of any party
organizations.offers: an online library of worksheets, videos, and guides for planning and running a campaign

organizations.name: New American Leaders
organizations.for: immigrants, refugees, and children of immigrants thinking about public office
organizations.offers: a weekend training on your stump speech, fundraising, and messaging; $150, with some scholarships

organizations.name: LGBTQ+ Victory Institute
organizations.for: LGBTQ+ people thinking about running, and the people who staff their campaigns
organizations.offers: a free one-day Candidate & Campaign 101 and multi-day campaign bootcamps (with a fee)

how_to_run.name: Virginia Department of Elections: becoming a candidate
how_to_run.offers: the step-by-step list for getting on a Virginia ballot: who qualifies, the forms, voter petitions, fees, and deadlines, with a guide for each office

how_to_run.name: New York State Board of Elections: running for office
how_to_run.offers: who can hold each office, the petition rules for party and independent candidates, and the filing calendar

how_to_run.name: NYC Board of Elections: for candidates
how_to_run.offers: petition forms and guidelines, the filing calendar, campaign finance reports, and where to file in each borough

how_to_run.name: NYC Campaign Finance Board: matching funds
how_to_run.offers: public money for city races: each NYC resident's donation is matched 8 to 1 on up to $250 ($175 for City Council), so small donations go much further

how_to_run.name: Virginia Beach Voter Registration & Elections: candidacy and campaign finance
how_to_run.offers: where to get candidate filing forms, a tool to check which election district you live in, when each local office is next on the ballot, and the campaign finance reporting rules

how_to_run.name: Chesapeake Voter Registrar: becoming a candidate
how_to_run.offers: the basic qualifications to run, with links to the state's candidate bulletin for each office, the filing forms, campaign finance reporting, and the city's political sign rules

how_to_run.name: Suffolk General Registrar: candidate resources and requirements
how_to_run.offers: who can run for city council and school board, which borough seats are on the ballot, how many petition signatures each office needs, and the city's rules for campaign finance and political signs

how_to_run.name: Gloucester Elections & Voter Registration: become a candidate
how_to_run.offers: when you can file to run, the campaign committee, bank account, and finance-report rules you'll have to follow, and a link to the state's full candidate guide

boards.name: Secretary of the Commonwealth: state boards and commissions
boards.offers: how to apply online for the roughly 900 seats the governor fills each year on state boards; most boards meet about four times a year

boards.name: Brooklyn Borough President: community boards
boards.offers: apply online or on paper to your Brooklyn community board; open to New Yorkers 16 and up, unpaid, about 6 to 8 hours a month; 2027 applications due Feb. 8, 2027

boards.name: Bronx Borough President: community boards
boards.offers: how Bronx community boards work and who gets appointed; unpaid seats, with applications reopening at the end of each year

boards.name: Manhattan Borough President: community boards
boards.offers: what Manhattan community board members do and how to apply; two-year unpaid terms, with a monthly board meeting and at least two committees

boards.name: Queens Borough President: community boards
boards.offers: how to join a Queens community board if you're 16 or older; unpaid two-year terms, with the next application period opening in early January 2027

boards.name: Staten Island Borough President: community board application
boards.offers: apply online or by mail to a Staten Island community board if you live, work, or have a stake in the district; 16- and 17-year-olds can apply

boards.name: Mayor's Office of Appointments: boards and commissions
boards.offers: the list of more than 200 city boards and commissions the mayor appoints, with a form to send your resume and say you want to serve

boards.name: City of Norfolk: apply for a board or commission
boards.offers: the current vacancy list and the online application for more than 50 city boards and commissions; City Council reviews applications every quarter and keeps them on file for a year

boards.name: City of Virginia Beach: Talent Bank application for boards and commissions
boards.offers: the application City Council draws from to fill seats on about 60 boards, commissions, and committees; open to Virginia Beach residents who are registered voters, and kept on file for five years

boards.name: City of Chesapeake: applicants needed for boards and commissions
boards.offers: the current list of open seats, application deadlines and the online application, which goes to the City Clerk

boards.name: City of Portsmouth: boards and commissions
boards.offers: what each city board and commission does, a link to the current vacancy list, and an application you can fill out online or print

boards.name: City of Suffolk: boards and commissions
boards.offers: the city's boards, commissions, and council committees; the page has no application, so ask the City Clerk's office, which handles appointments, at 757-514-4018 or council@suffolkva.us

boards.name: City of Newport News: boards, commissions and committees
boards.offers: how appointments to nearly 45 city boards work, with a link to the online Board Bank application; you must live in Newport News and pass a background check, and City Council appoints every quarter

boards.name: City of Williamsburg: boards and commissions
boards.offers: the online application for city residents to serve on city and regional boards; applications are taken any time and City Council reviews them when a seat opens

boards.name: City of Poquoson: boards and commissions
boards.offers: a printable Board Bank application for U.S. citizens registered to vote in Poquoson, covering 14 boards from the Planning Commission to the Wetlands Board; you turn it in, or a resume and cover letter, at the City Manager's Office

boards.name: York County: boards and commissions
boards.offers: the online Board Bank application, the list of current vacancies, and a guide to each board's requirements and meeting times; about 200 residents serve, appointed by the Board of Supervisors, and applications stay on file for a year

boards.name: Isle of Wight County: board and committee application
boards.offers: an online questionnaire for anyone who wants to serve on a county board, committee, or commission; questions go to County Administration at 757-365-6204

boards.name: Gloucester County: boards and commissions
boards.offers: a link to current vacancies and the application for the county's committees, councils, boards, and commissions, where more than 150 residents volunteer; questions go to County Administration at 804-693-4042

boards.name: Hampton Roads Planning District Commission: Community Advisory Committee
boards.offers: a printable application to join the up-to-30-member public committee that advises the region's planning and transportation boards; open to residents of the 17 member cities and counties, it meets six times a year, for three-year terms

boards.name: Hampton Roads Transit: Transit Riders Advisory Committee
boards.offers: a volunteer committee of up to 14 riders, with at least one from each city HRT serves, that tells HRT how to fix service problems; it meets every other month, and you ask HRT Customer Relations at 757-222-6000 about joining

boards.name: Hampton Roads Transit: Student Transit Riders Commission
boards.offers: an online application for high school students (grades 9 to 12) in the six cities HRT serves; a one-year term with a meeting every month

boards.name: NYC Civic Engagement Commission: Language Assistance Advisory Committee
boards.offers: a volunteer committee that advises the city's program of poll-site interpreters for voters with limited English; applications are taken on a rolling basis, members meet at least every three months, and speaking a second language helps but isn't required

boards.name: James City County: boards, commissions and other agencies
boards.offers: the county’s boards and commissions, with how to apply to serve on one

poll_work.name: Virginia Department of Elections: officers of election
poll_work.offers: how to sign up to work the polls anywhere in Virginia, with training before Election Day; pay depends on your role and your city or county, and the state says not every officer is paid

poll_work.name: New York State Board of Elections: become a poll worker
poll_work.offers: paid for training and for each day you work; you're assigned in your own county, and the sign-up form goes to your county board of elections

poll_work.name: NYC Board of Elections: poll worker positions
poll_work.offers: paid poll work as an inspector, interpreter, or 17-year-old poll worker; up to $2,750 for up to 10 days of work; apply online or on paper

poll_work.name: Norfolk Office of Elections: officer of election
poll_work.offers: the interest form for working Norfolk's polls; paid, with a $200 base rate that includes training and more for pollbook officers and chiefs; you stay the whole day, and polls are open 6 a.m. to 7 p.m.

poll_work.name: Virginia Beach Voter Registration & Elections: poll worker information
poll_work.offers: the online application to be an election official; $240 for Election Day plus $25 for a three-hour training; you must be 18 or older and a Virginia voter, and stay from 5 a.m. until the polls close and results are in

poll_work.name: Chesapeake Voter Registrar: working the polls
poll_work.offers: an interest form to work at a precinct near your home; $240 for Election Day and $25 for a training class, working from 5 a.m. until about 8 p.m.

poll_work.name: Portsmouth Voter Registration & Elections: becoming an election officer
poll_work.offers: the city's page for working the polls, with training videos; the city asks people who want to serve as an officer of election to contact the Registrar's office

poll_work.name: Suffolk Registrar: officer of election information
poll_work.offers: the online application to work the polls if you're a registered Virginia voter; $250 to $350 for Election Day depending on your role, plus $35 for training, from about 5 a.m. to 9 p.m.

poll_work.name: Newport News Voter Registrar: become an election official
poll_work.offers: the sign-up link for registered Virginia voters to work the polls from 5 a.m. until the count is done; $200 for an officer of election, up to $275 plus $20 for training for a chief officer

poll_work.name: Williamsburg Voter Registrar: working at the polls
poll_work.offers: how to become one of the 40-plus election officers the city needs for a general election, with full-day and half-day shifts; registered voters are paid $150, which covers a two-hour training class and Election Day

poll_work.name: Poquoson Voter Registration & Elections
poll_work.offers: the registrar's page, which links at the top to the state's sign-up form for election officials; it doesn't list pay or training, so call the office at 757-868-3070

poll_work.name: York County Voter Registration: election official information
poll_work.offers: a link to the state's sign-up form for working York County's polls; the page doesn't list pay or training

poll_work.name: Isle of Wight Voter Registration: officer of election information
poll_work.offers: the forms to apply as an officer of election in Isle of Wight County and a short Poll Working 101 video; the page doesn't list pay

poll_work.name: Gloucester Elections & Voter Registration: become an election officer
poll_work.offers: how to apply: pick up the forms at the Elections & Voter Registration office, and the Electoral Board will reply before the next election with training details if you're needed; the page doesn't list pay

poll_work.name: City of Hampton Voter Registrar: becoming an election official
poll_work.offers: how to become an officer of election (poll worker) in Hampton, from the city registrar

poll_work.name: James City County Voter Registration: becoming an election officer
poll_work.offers: how to sign up to work the polls as an officer of election in James City County
